title: Red Palm Weevil: Hidden Damage in Coconut and How to Stop It
metaTitle: Red Palm Weevil: Signs, Damage and Control
metaDescription: The red palm weevil grubs hollow out coconut trunks from inside. Learn the early warning signs, wound care and traps that protect your palms.
excerpt: The red palm weevil, Rhynchophorus ferrugineus, is a large reddish weevil whose grubs tunnel inside the trunk and crown of the palm. The damage stays hidden for a long time, and a hollowed palm can collapse. This page shows the early signs and the farm practices that keep it out.

blocks.text:
The red palm weevil is a large beetle with a long snout. Its grubs are legless, white with a brown head, and grow up to 50 mm long. They bore through the inside of the palm and make tunnels up to a meter long. It is native to southern Asia and Melanesia, and the Philippines is among the countries where it lives.

The weevil attacks coconut, betel nut, oil palm, sago palm, date palm and many ornamental palms. Palms can stand a lot of damage inside before any sign shows, and young palms under about 20 to 25 years are the most open to attack. So by the time the crown wilts, the trunk may already be hollow.

blocks.caption: Quick facts
rows: Stems and tillers and the whole plant
It attacks palms at any time of the year, and it enters through wounds from pruning, harvesting and other cuts in the trunk and the leaf bases.

The female lays 200 to 300 eggs in holes in the trunk or in the leaf stalks. The eggs hatch in a few days, and the grubs tunnel inside the palm for about 36 to 78 days. The full life cycle takes about 4 months.

blocks.text: How to Identify Red Palm Weevil

Look closely at the trunk, the base of the fronds and the crown. Tunnel holes with frass, a brown chewed paste, point to the weevil. Leaves with straight, cut looking edges instead of pointed tips are another sign. This weevil works inside the trunk. The [coconut rhinoceros beetle](/pests/coconut-rhinoceros-beetle) bores into the crown and leaves V shaped cuts in the leaves, so that is how you tell them apart.

items: Holes appear at the base of the fronds or in the trunk.
Frass sits at the entrance of the tunnels.
Leaflets show straight edges instead of pointed tips.
Leaves wilt and die, especially in the crown.
A badly attacked palm collapses because the inside is hollow.

blocks.title: Do not confuse it with
blocks.text: Wilting crowns can come from [coconut bud rot](/diseases/coconut-bud-rot) or from the rhinoceros beetle. Frass and tunnels in the trunk or the leaf bases point to the weevil.
How Red Palm Weevil Hurts Your Crop

The damage is inside, so farmers often see it late. Larvae can excavate tunnels up to 1 meter long, which weakens the palm until it dies. A pest that hides this well is cheaper to prevent than to cure.

A female lays 200 to 300 eggs, and the cycle takes only about 4 months. Numbers can build up fast inside one grove. Fresh wounds are the main door, so how you prune and harvest matters a lot.

The damage is not even everywhere. In India, CPCRI says it is serious only in certain pockets, mainly where the water table is high or where leaf rot and bud rot already weaken the palms. For large plantations, an Indian review of area wide programs assumes about 1 percent infested palms as the point to start action, and in small gardens farmers act on a single infested palm.
How to Control Red Palm Weevil

items: Remove and bury or destroy infested palms and trunks so the grubs cannot finish their life cycle. Cut and burn dead palms that still hold the pest.

Avoid cuts and injuries on the palm. When you cut green leaves, cut them about 120 cm from the base, and do not cut steps in the trunk for climbing, because the female lays eggs in cut and damaged tissue.
Clean the crown now and then so that rotting debris does not collect in the leaf axils.

Trap the adults. A coconut log split lengthwise, with fermented toddy on the cut face, attracts the weevils, and you collect and kill them each morning. A pheromone lure in a bucket trap baited with sugarcane also catches adults and tells you how many are around.
Treat palms with bud rot or leaf rot early, because weakened palms attract the weevil. Leave the natural enemies alone, since the assassin bug and earwigs eat the eggs and grubs.
Check palms often, because early treatment works better than late treatment, and one method alone seldom works when neighbors do nothing.

blocks.text: Trunk injection with fipronil or imidacloprid has been tried, but the Pacific fact sheet calls it uneconomical for coconut. Use a chemical only as advised by the PCA or a technician, and follow the label and the FPA registration.

blocks.title: Spray safely
blocks.text: Use only products registered with the [Fertilizer and Pesticide Authority](/blog/fertilizer-and-pesticide-authority), and follow the label for the rate, the timing and the protective clothing. Switch to a different insecticide group next time, so the pest does not learn to survive it. Our [guide to integrated pest management](/pests/integrated-pest-management) explains how.

items: Prune with care and keep the cuts small and clean.
Do not cut steps in the trunk for climbing.
Remove dying palms promptly so they do not become a breeding place.
Walk the grove often and look for frass, brown fluid at the holes and wilting crowns.

blocks.text: Questions Farmers Ask About Red Palm Weevil

items.q: Why do I see no damage until the palm collapses?
items.a: The grubs live and feed inside the palm. Palms can stand a lot of internal damage before symptoms show.

items.q: How does the weevil get into the palm?
items.a: The female lays eggs in wounds and in holes in the trunk or the leaf stalks. Pruning cuts, harvesting cuts and steps cut in the trunk for climbing are common entry points.

items.q: What can I do for a badly infested palm?
items.a: Remove and bury or destroy it, so the grubs cannot emerge and attack the next palm.
